claims.statement: Two entry points regenerate this repository's wiki and both run the same command, `openwiki code --update --print`: locally `mise run openwiki-update`, and in CI `.github/workflows/openwiki-update.yml`, which triggers on workflow_dispatch and a daily `cron: "0 8 * * *"`.

`mise run openwiki-update` is the one local generation entry point, including for a repository's very first wiki: `--update` handles the first run for code docs when env vars are set and, unlike `--init`, does not force the setup wizard, while `--print` makes it one-shot; the task runs the retry patch before every generation.

Every openwiki generator task is marked `interactive = true` because openwiki's UI is Ink and needs the real stdin/stdout: under mise's default output capture a prompt draws but cannot be answered, so it re-prompts forever.
All provider configuration for the openwiki mise tasks lives in ~/.config/harnessed/.env.schema, so the tasks are just `varlock run` — no task hard-codes a variable name or an endpoint.

The `openwiki_env` var strips the full provider surface from the environment with `env -u` ahead of `varlock run`, because varlock lets a process.env value override the schema: on 2026-09-04 stale `OPENWIKI_PROVIDER=openai-compatible` plus streaming exports repointed a 13-hour run at the wrong provider. The schema is the declared source of truth and a shell export must not outrank it — the same stance harnessed's host launcher takes.

The `env -u` list includes OPENWIKI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS because a shell export beats the schema: in run 7 (2026-09-08) an exported 32768 overrode the schema's 20000, and the @anthropic-ai/sdk client guard (_calculateNonstreamingTimeout: 3600*maxTokens/128000 > 600s) refuses any non-streaming call whose cap exceeds 21,333 — the planner is that one non-streaming call, so the run died there twice, the only failures in an otherwise clean 1.7h update.

`openwiki_env` passes `--filter` to varlock narrowing resolution to openwiki's own keys (`OPENWIKI_*,ANTHROPIC_*,LANGCHAIN_TRACING_V2,LANGSMITH_API_KEY`); without it a wiki run would also pull CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and the scanner tokens out of 1Password and export them into a process that talks to a third-party inference endpoint.

The openwiki mise tasks must run from main/, not from a worktree: docs/ is a gitignored live clone of the GitHub wiki, so a worktree checkout does not have it and the generated wiki would be written from an incomplete view of the project's own documentation.

`openwiki --init` walks every setup step unconditionally even in a fully configured environment — dist/cli/app/app.js:96 is `needsCredentialSetup(...) || (isInitCommand && !initWizardConsumed)` — so `mise run openwiki-init` exists only to reconfigure or to discard the generated wiki and start over; ordinary generation goes through openwiki-update.
`openwiki-visualize` deliberately skips varlock: it only serves the Markdown already on disk, so routing it through `varlock run` would touch 1Password for nothing.

`mise run openwiki-drift` runs tools/openwiki-drift.py with no model call, no network, and no varlock, which turns "which pages are lying" into a check rather than a regeneration — the cheap thing to run before deciding to run openwiki-update; its gate semantics are documented in testing/verification-ladder.md.
The mise pin for openwiki is 0.5.1, the version verified against this tree (2026-09-16); `latest` would make the provider env-var contract an unpinned assumption.

The openwiki tool entry in mise.toml carries `allow_builds = ["better-sqlite3"]` because mise installs through aube, which denies dependency lifecycle scripts by default — denied, the install still reports success and every openwiki run dies at "Could not locate the bindings file" (better-sqlite3 reaches openwiki transitively through @langchain/langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite, still in 0.5.1). trust_policy_excludes is GONE: it covered fastq@1.20.2, which shipped no provenance attestation, but fastq 1.20.3 is attested again and every `^` range in the 0.5.1 tree resolves there; if a later unattested fastq lands, the install fails loudly at resolve time and the exclude should be re-added with that exact version.

A page worker whose stream ends without calling submit_page is marked skipped by openwiki, the page snapshot is restored, and the run finalizes "interrupted" without advancing the diff base. Observed with glm-5.3-flash: 94 LLM calls, a clean exit, no tool call, no error (PR #445 run 6). No release through 0.5.1 retries a skipped page — 0.5.1's runPageAgent carries the same try/skip block byte-for-byte as 0.4.3. 0.5.0's durable page manifest (openwiki/.page-manifest.json) softens the cost — a completed page is no longer regenerated — but a skip still leaves the run interrupted.

tools/openwiki-retry-patch.py gives each page worker one fresh second attempt before the page is skipped: it rewrites runPageAgent in the installed dist/agent/repository-runner.js (version-gated to exactly 0.5.1), converting the single `const agent = createDeepAgent({...})` into a `createWorkerAgent` factory wrapped in a two-attempt loop; the retry shares the worker's virtual backend so attempt 2 sees the page markdown attempt 1 already wrote, a first miss emits a named retry event, and only a second miss falls through to skipRepositoryPage plus the deferred warning exactly as stock code does.

The retry patch fails loudly rather than patching blind: it refuses any install whose version is not the verified 0.4.3, and it exits when its anchors — runPageAgent, exactly one agent declaration, exactly one worker try-block — are not found exactly once, with the message "anchor drift, re-derive the patch". Version drift means a human re-derives the patch against the new layout; the tool never patches blind.

The retry patch is idempotent and reversible: a marker identifies an already-patched runner, `--check` reports patched state (exit 0/1) without touching anything, `--revert` restores the `.orig` backup, and every write is followed by a `node --check` syntax check.

The workflow checks out with `fetch-depth: 0` because `openwiki code --update` diffs HEAD against the commit it last documented — a shallow clone hides that commit and the update runs against an empty change summary — and with `persist-credentials: false` because the openwiki step runs third-party code over the whole repository: persisted git credentials would sit in the job's git config for it to find, and create-pull-request takes its own token input and does not read them.

CI installs openwiki@0.5.1 with `npm install --global` (plus mermaid and jsdom for high-fidelity Mermaid validation), deliberately not the recipe's project-scoped pnpm install: the runner has no strictDepBuilds policy, and npm 10/11 still runs dependency lifecycle scripts by default, so better-sqlite3 builds with no allowlist at all.

A dedicated verify step searches the global node_modules for better_sqlite3.node and fails with the fix in the error message (npm 12 blocks dependency lifecycle scripts by default; add --allow-scripts=better-sqlite3, or install via pnpm with an allowBuilds entry as the recipe does), because openwiki imports SqliteSaver at module load, so a missing native addon breaks every subcommand — surfacing as "Could not locate the bindings file" mid-generation rather than as a failed install.

The openwiki step in CI is deliberately not fail-fast (`continue-on-error: true`): the page-job queue is durable, so a run that dies partway has already written every page it finished and the create-pull-request step banks that progress as the next run's baseline; the last step re-raises when `steps.openwiki.outcome == 'failure'` so the job still reports red.

The create-pull-request step runs `if: ${{ always() }}` — not `!cancelled()` — because timeout-minutes kills the job with cancelled() == true, and skipping the PR step on a timeout would discard every page the durable queue wrote. `add-paths` limits the PR to openwiki, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and the workflow itself, the branch is `openwiki/update`, and the PR body states that a `failure` result intentionally preserves only the pages completed before the failure, directing reviewers to `mise run openwiki-drift` before merging; a final step re-raises exit 1 when steps.openwiki.outcome == 'failure' so the job still reports red. `sign-commits: true` is required by the branch ruleset's verified-signature demand: without it the plain-git commit was unmergeable (#482 sat blocked), and the action instead creates the commit via the GitHub API, signed server-side with GitHub's own key (authored by github-actions[bot]) so no signing key is stored in Actions secrets.

The CI generation step runs OPENWIKI_PROVIDER=anthropic against z.ai's Anthropic-compatible face (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL https://api.z.ai/api/anthropic, model glm-5.2) — not the OpenAI-compatible face, whose non-streaming HTTP dies at undici's 300s headersTimeout and whose streaming flag was broken through 0.5.0; the Anthropic client streams SSE by default so long glm turns survive (verified in PR #445 run 8). OPENWIKI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS is now explicitly set to "20000" and is required: the @anthropic-ai/sdk non-streaming timeout guard refuses the planner's call above 21,333, while too low a cap returns HTTP 200 with empty content — a silently blank page — because glm draws reasoning tokens from the completion budget.

The workflow sets no LANGCHAIN_TRACING_V2: that variable gates openwiki's interactive setup wizard (setup/credentials/steps.js), which additionally requires a TTY (cli/app/app.js) that CI does not have, so it is needed for a terminal run and redundant in CI.

openwiki/.run.json — the resumable-run checkpoint — is gitignored in this repository while the generated wiki itself (openwiki/*.md and openwiki/.claims/) is committed, because a half-finished run's queue state is meaningless in any other checkout; consequently, unlike upstream's scheduled-workflow example, the CI workflow needs no transient run-state cleanup before opening its PR.

.openwikiignore is the read boundary for wiki runs: paths listed there are never read, scanned, or reproduced in the generated wiki — and tests/ and tools/ are deliberately kept readable because that is where this project's contracts are pinned; the rationale lives in the file.

The .openwikiignore exclusions .claude/worktrees/ and docs/codebase/ each block evidence that would launder wrongness into the wiki: agent task worktrees are full checkouts of the same repository on divergent branches, so left readable openwiki would ground Claims in dozens of divergent copies of every file it documents, and docs/codebase/ is the output of an older /map-codebase run, so grounding on it turns "the map said so" into evidence — exactly the drift openwiki's Claims exist to catch — while the hand-written docs/guides/ and docs/harnessed-design.md stay readable.

tests/ and tools/ are deliberately not in the read boundary because that is where the project's contracts are pinned — mise.toml cites test_external_contracts_live.py by name as the reason varlock is pinned, and install.sh precedence is asserted as order in test_install_script.py::TestPrecedence — and the tools/ exclusion was narrowed back to the generated fixture profiles it was meant to cover (tools/test-fixtures/profiles/) because excluding the whole directory made the wiki describe tools/run-tests.sh, tools/preflight.sh and tools/openwiki-drift.py from mise.toml and the CI workflows alone, which is how testing/verification-ladder.md came to overstate what the drift gate verifies (raised in review on #445).

The remaining .openwikiignore entries are derivations and noise, not project source: build and analysis artifacts (/profiles/, catalog-local/, mutants/, tool caches), editor and agent state (.serena/, .vscode/, .agents/, and the .claude/ remainder whose consequential half is the worktrees entry), web/ as unrelated to the shipped project, catalog/recipes.backlog (PLAN.md drafts for recipes that do not exist yet, which would describe capabilities the catalog lacks), and uv.lock as a machine-generated dependency graph with no prose signal.

The retry patch locates the runner over two mise-install globs because pnpm 11 symlinks node_modules/openwiki into the content-addressable store under ~/.pnpm-store/v11/links/ and emits sibling hash directories that all realpath to the same store path — matches are realpath-de-duplicated and ambiguity is an error. On the pnpm 11 layout the patched file lives in the shared store, so any other project resolving openwiki@0.5.1 to the same hash sees the patch too; there is no project-local copy to patch instead.

The retry patch runs in CI too, not only locally: the workflow applies tools/openwiki-retry-patch.py to the npm-global install with an explicit path (`$(npm root -g)/openwiki/dist/agent/repository-runner.js`), and the patch is idempotent plus version-gated so it refuses anything but 0.5.1; verified 2026-09-16 that the npm-global patched runner is byte-identical to the locally patched one.

tools/openwiki-drift.py verifies only line-ranged evidence anchors (repo://path#Lx-Ly) by recomputing the repo-lines-v1 sha256 digest of the selected lines against the working tree; whole-file evidence (no #L) and Claims using unknown version schemes (e.g. a future repo-lines-v2) are skipped and reported separately rather than guessed at, so the gate cannot go quietly green on unverified evidence. It re-finds moved-but-identical blocks by scanning for a window of the recorded line count whose digest matches and reports them as moved, not drift; only a changed digest or a missing file exits 1, and malformed wiki/Claims exit 2.

tools/run-tests.sh runs the test suite correctly from any worktree by handling three local-only failure modes: it runs `mise trust` (a no-op once trusted), syncs the per-branch venv with `--extra dev` because pytest is an optional dev extra that a plain `uv sync` omits, and then `exec`s `uv run pytest` with any passed args (defaulting to `-q`). It deliberately does not strip FORCE_COLOR — tests/conftest.py pops it at import, the only place early enough before rich Consoles are constructed at module import.

openwiki-drift reports relocated evidence whose #Lx-Ly span was not rewritten as a separate `staleURI` count, distinct from drift, because openwiki does not update the resource URI when it relocates a block; the recorded selectedLineCount in the version payload is authoritative for the digest's window length and wins over the URI span.
